questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: How can a motorcycle rider improve their visibility?
questions.explanation: Wear bright-colored clothing with reflective materials so other drivers can see you. Always use your headlight, signals, and brake light.

questions.question: What is often found in the center of a lane?
questions.explanation: Oil and grease from cars drip and form a strip in the center of each lane. When it is dry, a motorcycle can usually ride safely on this strip.

questions.question: How can a motorcycle rider slow down?
questions.explanation: Riders can slow down by downshifting. Be aware that downshifting does not turn on the brake lights.

questions.question: How long does a pre-ride inspection take?

options.text: A few minutes and should be done no more than once a month.
A few minutes and should be done before every ride.
Over an hour and should be performed by a mechanic.
Over an hour and must only be done if you will be carrying a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: A few minutes and should be done before every ride.
questions.explanation: Do a pre-ride inspection before every ride. It usually takes only a few minutes.

questions.question: What type of sign is rectangular?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs, such as speed limit signs, are rectangular with white background and black lettering. Riders must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: What should a motorcycle rider do on a slippery surface?
questions.explanation: Slow down on slippery surfaces. Sudden moves can cause your motorcycle to skid. Do not ride on the shoulder to avoid a slippery road.

questions.question: What reduces the risk of head or neck injury in a crash?

options.text: Not allowing a passenger on the motorcycle

questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet is the best way to reduce the risk of head or neck injuries in a crash.

questions.question: Under normal conditions, where should you ride in your lane?

options.text: The left portion of the lane.
The center portion of the lane.
The right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Normally ride in the center of the lane when there are no hazards. Be ready to change your lane position as conditions change.

questions.question: What should you do if someone is tailgating you?

options.text: Ride on the shoulder of the road.

questions.explanation: Let the tailgater pass. Change lanes safely and let them get in front of you. Riding faster can increase danger by encouraging them to tailgate at higher speeds.

questions.question: Slippery surfaces make it hard to control a motorcycle. Which surface is slippery?
questions.explanation: Wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal plates in the road are all slippery. Ride with extra caution on these surfaces.

questions.question: To get the most protection, choose a helmet that:
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards. The helmet should fit snugly all the way around your head.

questions.question: When should you inspect your motorcycle before riding?
questions.explanation: Inspect your motorcycle before every ride. Small technical problems on a motorcycle can be more dangerous than on a car.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Travel on the shoulder away from other traffic.

questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, use both brakes gently, reduce your speed, and avoid sudden moves. Watch for oily areas, shaded areas, dirt, gravel, and bridges—these have less traction.

questions.question: The shortest and safest stops happen when you:

options.text: Allow the front tire to lock up.
Use both the front and rear brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both the front and rear brakes smoothly and gradually. Do not lock up either tire.

questions.question: Which surface is NOT slippery?
questions.explanation: Slippery surfaces include wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal plates. Dry pavement provides good traction.

questions.question: When riding, you should:

options.text: Always look ahead and watch for potential dangers.
Focus on the controls and speedometer instead of the road.
Not worry about hazards because there are very few on the road.
Look ahead but don't look for hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always look ahead and watch for potential dangers.
questions.explanation: Look well ahead of your motorcycle. This helps you spot dangers early and react before you reach them.

questions.question: Which item is NOT protective clothing for a motorcyclist?
questions.explanation: Wear protective clothing including sturdy jackets and pants that cover your arms and legs, boots that support your ankles, and sturdy gloves.

questions.question: Most motorcycles have:

options.text: Brakes in both the front and rear.
Three brakes: front, rear, and emergency.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brakes in both the front and rear.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have two brakes: one for the front wheel and one for the rear wheel.

questions.question: During the day, you should:

options.text: Use your headlight only when it is cloudy.
Use your headlight only if you want to.

questions.explanation: Always ride with your headlight on, even during the day. This makes other drivers twice as likely to notice you.

questions.question: Keep extra space between your motorcycle and the vehicle in front of you:

options.text: When stopping will be harder than usual.
When you want to look at the scenery.
To encourage other drivers to cut you off.
To prevent the driver in front of you from knowing you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: When stopping will be harder than usual.
questions.explanation: Keep extra space if your motorcycle needs longer to stop. Leave more distance on slippery pavement, when you cannot see ahead, or when traffic is heavy and another driver may cut in front of you.

questions.question: If you borrow a motorcycle:

options.text: Don't worry about checking the tire pressure.
Expect it to handle the same as your own bike.
The lender will make sure the brakes work so you don't have to.
Leave extra space when riding to give yourself more time to react.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave extra space when riding to give yourself more time to react.
questions.explanation: Check the borrowed motorcycle the same way you check your own bike before riding. Ride carefully on an unfamiliar motorcycle and allow yourself extra space for stopping.

questions.question: Unlike most food and drinks, alcohol does not need to be digested. This means:

options.text: Alcohol reaches the brain within minutes and starts to affect you.
It takes a long time to feel the effects of alcohol.
Your body gets rid of alcohol very quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol reaches the brain within minutes and starts to affect you.
questions.explanation: Alcohol does not need digestion, so it enters your bloodstream quickly and reaches your brain within minutes. Your body eliminates about one drink per hour.

questions.question: One benefit of regular motorcycle maintenance is:

options.text: Your motorcycle will ride well for a long time.
The maintenance check will take a lot of time.
Maintenance checks can prevent parking tickets.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your motorcycle will ride well for a long time.
questions.explanation: A well-maintained motorcycle will ride like new if you perform routine inspections and maintenance regularly.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle on a slippery surface, you should:
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, reduce your speed. Use both brakes when braking and avoid sudden movements.
